artifacts.summary: 13-phase plan splitting StarAxiom.ofBase into 53 schematic mirror constructors (modal_future alone under RecallFree), retiring ofBase and stabNecessitationOfPlus, re-proving validity and swap-validity per arm, and re-verifying conservativity.

memory_candidates.content: Retiring a monolithic constructor from a wildcard-free inductive dispatch (Lean: an axiom inductive matched by minFrameClass plus two no-wildcard dispatch lemmas) cannot be phased as 'replace the constructor, then supply the arms' -- the build is red for the whole interval, which is irreconcilable with a commit-per-green-substep mandate. The decomposition that works is ADD FIRST, DELETE LAST: keep the monolith as a temporary in-task scaffold while the replacement constructors land in swap-closed groups, each group landing its constructors, its frame-class arms and both dispatch arms in one green commit; then delete the monolith in a single atomic-batch phase together with every consumer rewrite. Two further structure points make the retirement real rather than cosmetic: (a) the embedding the monolith provided returns as a DERIVED function over the new constructors (provable, adds nothing to the system) rather than as a residual constructor; (b) the frame-class agreement between old and new routing is proved as ONE named cases lemma, so a mismatch is a named failure at a single site instead of N silent inline rfl's. Group the new constructors so each group is closed under the system's duality operation, or a group's swap arms will need a validity lemma from a later phase.
